review_note: Which canonical result quantities each engine can produce at all. A source quantity outside an engine's set is not a missing counterpart -- the engine has no such state to report -- so it is reported as engine-incapable and kept out of that engine's parity denominator. This is deliberately narrow: a quantity the engine CAN produce but did not is still a blocker, because that is a real gap in the run. Adding a quantity here is a claim that the engine genuinely has no such output, not that a comparison was inconvenient.

cannot_produce.excitation_voltage: OpenDSS's generator dynamics model has no field circuit, so there is no excitation voltage state to report.
cannot_produce.electrical_torque: OpenDSS reports shaft and electrical power; torque is not a state its generator model exposes.
cannot_produce.mechanical_torque: OpenDSS reports shaft power (PShaft), not mechanical torque.
cannot_produce.rotor_angle: Monitor mode 3 exposes speed and shaft power; the machine's own rotor angle is not among its reported states.
cannot_produce.relative_rotor_angle: Requires a reference machine angle, which OpenDSS does not report for any machine.
cannot_produce.internal_rotor_angle: PowerFactory's internal machine angle has no OpenDSS equivalent state.
cannot_produce.external_rotor_angle: PowerFactory's external machine angle has no OpenDSS equivalent state.
cannot_produce.rotor_position_d: Rotor position referred to the reference bus voltage is not an OpenDSS generator state.
cannot_produce.rotor_position_x: Rotor position from the machine state vector is not an OpenDSS generator state.

asset_rules.reason: OpenDSS models the reference machine as an ideal voltage source, which has no machine states at all -- no speed, no angle, no shaft power.
